songs.title: Old Exit
songs.centralImage: the station exit leading into the old neighborhood
songs.genreText: CHILI LAB chill rap with restrained trip-hop shading
songs.stylePrompt: CHILI LAB chill rap / trip-hop, 72 BPM; loose broken kick and rim, baritone guitar, soft bass, faint Wurlitzer. Smoky female contralto, dark low chest, behind-the-beat narrative rap, compact melodic hook. Three-note guitar answer after the title. Full three-verse arrangement; preserve all three hook passes.
songs.excludePrompt: glossy chill house, dominant Rhodes, trap hats, bright pop chorus, falsetto climax, hard snare, giant stack, artist imitation, copied melody
songs.lyrics:
[Intro - 8 bars instrumental]

[Verse 1 - 16 bars, low rap]
Same station name, different ticket gate,
you say the old exit moved two doors east.
A florist took the place of the newspaper stand,
the clock above the stairs is five minutes slow.
Yesterday we talked until the screen went dim,
today the air feels easier than the messages did.
You point past the taxis toward a narrow lane,
and say the real neighborhood starts that way.
A delivery truck blocks half the crossing,
a school uniform flashes through the crowd.
You know which signal changes too quickly,
which corner keeps rain longer after noon.
I know none of it yet, which is the point,
so I let you choose the first small turn.

[Pre-Hook - 4 bars]
No map, no plan, no reason to hurry,
you know every turn before it arrives.

[Hook 1 - 8 bars, melodic]
This Way First,
show me where the small streets start.
This Way First,
let the main road disappear behind us.

[Post-Hook - 4 bars]
This way first,
then whatever comes after.

[Verse 2 - 16 bars, low rap]
Corner pharmacy changed its sign twice,
the noodle shop still keeps chairs outside.
You tell me which crossing felt enormous at nine,
which alley looked longer walking home alone.
A cracked mirror hangs by a bicycle shop,
three plastic stools wait under a red vent.
You say there used to be a payphone here,
and everybody knew whose coins went missing.
I tell you my street had one just like it,
different city, same scratched metal shelf.
The more specific your memories become,
the less I need to ask what they mean.

[Hook 2 - 8 bars, melodic]
This Way First,
past the shop with the crooked sign.
This Way First,
one old story at a time.

[Bridge - 8 bars, low rap]
You stop once, turn back half a step,
then choose the lane behind the bakery.
I ask how you still remember all this.
You say your feet remember before you do.
That line stays with the beat for a while,
baritone guitar answering underneath.

[Verse 3 - 12 bars, low rap]
Now the station noise is gone behind us,
replaced by dishes, scooters, window fans.
You point at places without explaining first,
and I start recognizing them from your stories.
Blue gate ahead, school wall after that,
a clock that never learned the right time.
This is not my neighborhood, not yet,
but I can already follow the order.

[Final Hook - 12 bars, melodic]
This Way First,
now it sounds less like directions.
This Way First,
the old street opens one turn at a time.
This Way First,
I know enough now to keep walking.

[Outro Motif - 4 bars instrumental]

durationDesign.method: three full verses + three hook passes + lyric bridge; not dependent on instrumental break

killingPointDesign.mechanism: three-note baritone-guitar answer plus final-hook meaning shift
killingPointDesign.finalVariation: direction phrase becomes a trust phrase

songs.title: Still Blue
songs.centralImage: a faded blue gate with an old apartment number
songs.genreText: soft 2-step garage carrying CHILI LAB sing-rap
songs.stylePrompt: CHILI LAB soft 2-step / urban soul, 104 BPM; shuffled kick-snare, ghost percussion, Wurlitzer stabs, rubbery bass, reverse guitar tails. Warm male tenor-baritone, forward chest-mix, syncopated sing-rap verse, compact hook. Two-note reverse-guitar answer after 'Blue'. Full three-verse arrangement; keep all hook passes.
songs.excludePrompt: festival garage, aggressive bass, straight deep house, bright pop tenor, hard sidechain, giant stack, artist imitation, copied melody
songs.lyrics:
[Intro - 8 bars instrumental]

[Verse 1 - 16 bars, sing-rap]
Number nine is smaller than you remember,
blue paint gone pale around the latch.
You say the second-floor window was yours,
then laugh because the curtain style is somehow the same.
A delivery bike leans where a scooter used to sit,
mailboxes replaced but the concrete stayed.
You once hid report cards in that stairwell,
behind a pipe nobody thought to check.
The building name lost two metal letters,
one screw still marks where the first one hung.
You tell the story fast, then slow it down,
as if the doorway is correcting details.

[Pre-Hook - 8 bars]
No need to ring, no need to go inside,
we only borrow the view from the sidewalk.
The paint changed shade, the number stayed,
that is enough for one stop today.

[Hook 1 - 12 bars, melodic]
Still Blue,
not the same blue, still enough.
Still Blue,
one old color holding its place.
Still Blue,
the latch remembers more than the sign.

[Post-Hook - 4 bars]
Still blue,
still here.

[Verse 2 - 16 bars, sing-rap]
You point to a crack near the bottom hinge,
say a bicycle pedal put it there one summer.
A neighbor used to leave shoes by the meter,
a radio played through an open kitchen screen.
You knew dinner by the smell from downstairs,
and knew trouble by how quiet the landing got.
The story is small, almost nothing,
but you tell it without editing the ending.
I say my building had a stairwell echo,
seven floors of doors that all sounded different.
You ask which one was mine, and for once
I answer before changing the subject.

[Hook 2 - 12 bars, melodic]
Still Blue,
not the same blue, still enough.
Still Blue,
two old buildings in one conversation.
Still Blue,
the sidewalk makes room for both.

[Bridge - 12 bars, sing-rap]
We do not need the old key,
do not need anyone to let us in.
A faded gate can do its work from here,
showing what stayed and what learned to leave.
Reverse guitar turns the title backward,
then drops it gently into the next beat.

[Verse 3 - 16 bars, sing-rap]
Before we go, you count the windows,
second floor, third from the left.
You thought the room was bigger,
thought the street below was twice as wide.
I tell you memory has bad measurements,
you say maybe that is why it fits so much.
We start walking before the sentence ends,
leaving the blue gate where it always was.

[Final Hook - 16 bars, melodic]
Still Blue,
[Female low response: still there]
not the same blue, still enough.
Still Blue,
one old color, two new stories.
Still Blue,
we do not have to go inside.
Still Blue.

[Outro - 4 bars instrumental]

durationDesign.method: three lyric-heavy sing-rap verses, three hooks, post-hook and bridge; high BPM protected with real vocal content

killingPointDesign.mechanism: female one-line response plus reverse-guitar answer
killingPointDesign.finalVariation: final hook widens from one childhood to two

songs.title: Four Ten
songs.centralImage: the bakery clock that marked after-school bread time
songs.genreText: acoustic bossa-soulhop with a CHILI LAB melodic center
songs.stylePrompt: CHILI LAB bossa-soulhop, 88 BPM; nylon guitar, upright bass, soft cross-stick, vibraphone, sparse piano. Clear female mezzo, conversational sung verses, compact hook, warm low-energy harmony. Four-note clocklike vibraphone motif after the title. Full three-verse song form; preserve three distinct hook passes and bridge.
songs.excludePrompt: tropical house, samba party percussion, deep-house kick, bright idol vocal, belt, giant harmony stack, artist imitation, copied melody
songs.lyrics:
[Intro - 8 bars instrumental]

[Verse 1 - 16 bars, sung]
The bakery clock is stuck at four-ten,
even though the wall clock inside says five.
You laugh and say four-ten was the real time anyway,
the minute school let go and coins became bread.
Sweet bean, sugar twist, whatever was cheapest,
three friends deciding like it mattered all week.
The owner has changed, the trays have changed,
but warm air still reaches halfway down the lane.
You remember the paper bag going soft with steam,
and crumbs collecting in the fold of your sleeve.
I can almost see the uniform jackets,
though none of those people are standing here now.

[Hook 1 - 8 bars]
Four Ten,
the hour after the last school bell.
Four Ten,
one small clock refusing to grow up.

[Post-Hook - 4 bars]
Four-ten, four-ten,
vibraphone counts it back.

[Verse 2 - 16 bars, sung]
I tell you my version from another town,
a corner store and frozen juice in summer.
Different street, almost the same rule:
go home slowly until the lights come on.
We used to stretch five minutes into twenty,
stand by a vending machine and call it a plan.
You say that sounds exactly like your group,
only yours had bread instead of colored ice.
For the first time on this walk,
the story belongs to both sides of the conversation.
Two separate maps line up for a moment,
right where the bakery door keeps opening.

[Hook 2 - 8 bars]
Four Ten,
your clock, my corner store.
Four Ten,
two ways of taking the long road home.

[Bridge - 12 bars, sung]
The clerk lifts another tray from the back,
and the whole lane changes temperature.
You say the smell is almost right,
I say almost is probably the honest version.
The clock above us does not move,
which makes it better at remembering.

[Verse 3 - 16 bars, sung]
We buy one small roll and split it,
not because the story needs a souvenir.
It is simply warm and we are standing here,
and the evening has not asked us to leave.
You take the first bite, call it different,
then take another before deciding how different.
I tell you that is not a fair review,
you say childhood was never known for standards.
The stuck clock watches all of this,
patient as a photograph no one has taken.

[Final Hook - 16 bars]
Four Ten,
[Delayed entrance] four-ten, still there.
Four Ten,
the hour after somebody lets you go.
Four Ten,
your bread, my frozen juice, same slow rule.
Four Ten,
the vibraphone finishes what the clock cannot.

[Outro Motif - 8 bars instrumental]

durationDesign.method: three sung verses, three hooks, post-hook and bridge; song-centered track no longer has a natural ending after verse two

killingPointDesign.mechanism: delayed final title entrance plus four-note clock motif
killingPointDesign.finalVariation: two childhood routines merge in the last hook

songs.lyrics:
[Intro - 8 bars instrumental]

[Verse 1 - 16 bars, low rap]
School wall got a new coat last spring,
you can tell by the cleaner line near the drain.
You say there used to be chalk squares here,
four boxes for a game nobody plays now.
One corner still shows through the paint,
white line under grey if the light hits sideways.
You crouch just enough to point, then stand,
like proof only matters for a second.
The fence is taller than you remember,
the trees inside are somehow lower.
A basketball hits somewhere beyond the building,
not the same game, close enough to echo.

[Pre-Hook - 4 bars]
New paint covers most things well,
not everything agrees to disappear.

[Hook 1 - 8 bars]
Still Under There,
one pale line below the grey.
Still Under There,
not asking anyone to remember.

[Verse 2 - 16 bars, low rap]
You tell me who always cheated at the game,
who ran home first when the rain began.
Who could jump the longest chalk line,
who carried a ruler and changed the rules.
Names come easy because none need an ending,
just enough detail to bring back the wall.
I tell you my school had painted numbers,
blue ones fading under newer white.
Different marks, same argument with time,
cover it once, it keeps showing through.

[Hook 2 - 8 bars]
Still Under There,
not the line, the way you tell it.
Still Under There,
something pale beneath the new coat.

[Bridge - 8 bars, low rap]
A teacher walks past on the other side,
does not know why we are looking down.
That feels right. The wall does not need witnesses,
just evening light at the correct angle.
Muted trumpet falls three notes,
leaves the last one almost unresolved.

[Verse 3 - 12 bars, low rap]
We follow the wall toward the next corner,
where the chalk disappears for good.
You do not try to find another piece,
and I do not ask you to.
One surviving line was enough
to open five more stories on the way.

[Final Hook - 12 bars]
Still Under There,
final title nearly spoken.
Still Under There,
not everything needs to show clearly.
Still Under There,
trumpet leaves one note unfinished.

[Outro - 4 bars instrumental]

killingPointDesign.mechanism: near-spoken final title plus unresolved trumpet reply
killingPointDesign.finalVariation: image shifts from chalk line to memory itself

songs.title: Three Coins
songs.centralImage: three coins once used at a tiny candy shop
songs.genreText: minimal neo-soul chill rap with dry pocket
songs.stylePrompt: CHILI LAB minimal neo-soul chill rap, 84 BPM; dry rim clicks, Hammond, fretless bass, tremolo guitar. Mature male tenor-baritone, warm chest, conversational sing-rap verse, restrained hook. Fretless slide and Hammond answer the title. Full three-verse arrangement; retain three hook passes and lyric bridge.
songs.excludePrompt: Rhodes-led alt-R&B, gospel runs, falsetto climax, octave jump, hard snare, bright pop chorus, artist imitation, copied melody
songs.lyrics:
[Intro - 8 bars instrumental]

[Verse 1 - 16 bars, sing-rap]
Tiny shop still has the same narrow door,
new refrigerator, same bell overhead.
You say three coins once made a whole afternoon:
one sour candy, one soda, one bad decision.
You kept the change in the smallest coat pocket,
and sometimes lost it before the corner.
The story gets funnier every sentence,
mostly because you stop trying to tell it well.
You knew which shelf the owner watched,
which jar was safer to point at than touch.
Three coins clicked together like a budget,
serious business at ten years old.

[Pre-Hook - 4 bars]
Small metal, enormous plans,
three sounds against the pocket lining.

[Hook 1 - 8 bars]
Three Coins,
all the way to the end of the block.
Three Coins,
more than enough for an afternoon.

[Verse 2 - 16 bars, sing-rap]
I tell you about a red vending machine in my town,
where one button always ate the change.
We kicked the bottom like that was a strategy,
then blamed the machine for knowing our names.
Different childhood, same bad arithmetic,
and now we are laughing too loudly for the shop.
The owner glances up, then back down,
probably used to people buying memory with snacks.
You find a coin under a receipt in your bag,
hold it up like evidence the story kept going.

[Hook 2 - 8 bars]
Three Coins,
one for you and one for me.
Three Coins,
leave the last one for the next bad idea.

[Bridge - 8 bars, sing-rap]
We buy nothing that matters,
two small candies and a bottle to share.
Fretless bass slides up under the title,
Hammond answers down without getting louder.
The whole scene stays pocket-sized,
which is exactly why it works.

[Verse 3 - 16 bars, sing-rap]
Outside, the bell closes behind us,
and the lane feels cooler than the shop.
You unwrap yours carefully at the seam,
I tear mine wrong and lose half the paper.
You say that would have bothered you at ten,
I say it still bothers you now.
That earns me one very specific look,
then another story about saving wrappers.
Three coins become three more blocks,
and we keep walking before finishing the candy.

[Final Hook - 12 bars]
Three Coins,
[Female low response: spend one]
three little sounds against the pocket lining.
Three Coins,
one afternoon, then another one.
Three Coins.

[Outro - 4 bars instrumental]

durationDesign.method: three sing-rap verses, three hooks, bridge and real post-story progression

killingPointDesign.finalVariation: coins shift from childhood budget to present walk

songs.title: Twelve Steps
songs.centralImage: a twelve-step stone staircase used as a childhood shortcut
songs.genreText: acoustic soul-hop with clear CHILI LAB rap delivery
songs.stylePrompt: CHILI LAB acoustic soul-hop / chill rap, 92 BPM; fingerpicked steel guitar, upright bass, brushed snare, small percussion, cello. Clear female alto, open chest, light rhythmic rap, short sung hook. Guitar harmonics mark the count; cello answers upward. Full three-verse arrangement; keep all three hooks.
songs.excludePrompt: bright folk-pop strum, Rhodes bed, deep-house kick, gang vocals, falsetto lead, cinematic strings, artist imitation, copied melody
songs.lyrics:
[Intro - 8 bars instrumental]

[Verse 1 - 16 bars, light rap]
One, two, three, fourth step cracked,
you remember that before we even reach it.
Five through eight are narrower than they looked,
nine has moss where somebody fixed the edge.
You say twelve used to feel like a mountain
with a school bag and wet shoes in July.
Now we reach the top before the story ends,
so we stand by the rail and finish it there.
A small shrine sits behind a new fence,
a mailbox moved from left to right.
You swear step seven used to tilt more,
then test it twice like the stone owes you proof.

[Hook 1 - 8 bars, sung]
Count Them Again,
old steps, smaller legs, same hill.
Count Them Again,
twelve is still twelve from here.

[Verse 2 - 16 bars, light rap]
You used to race the last four steps,
never the first eight because that was cheating.
A friend always started too soon,
another stopped halfway to fix a shoe.
I tell you which staircase scared me as a kid,
not this city, not this shape, same stupid fear.
You say that is close enough to understand,
and the next story comes without a question.
We compare which step felt worst in rain,
which rail froze hardest in winter.
The details overlap without matching,
which makes the conversation better.

[Hook 2 - 8 bars]
Count Them Again,
one for then and one for now.
Count Them Again,
twelve little beats under the shoes.

[Bridge - 12 bars, rap]
At the top, we look back down,
the staircase suddenly ordinary from above.
You say that is unfair to the memory,
I say memory always shoots from below.
Guitar harmonics count four small notes,
cello answers with one long rise.
No need to make the hill bigger,
it already carried the story here.

[Verse 3 - 16 bars, light rap]
We take the steps down slower than we climbed,
not counting until step four by accident.
Then you start at five and I join at six,
seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve.
You say we counted backward badly,
I say the street will forgive us.
At the bottom another lane opens,
and the school wall disappears behind the houses.

[Final Hook - 16 bars]
Count Them Again,
this time the guitar answers twelve.
Count Them Again,
old steps, new voices, same hill.
Count Them Again,
we are already walking before the last note ends.

[Outro - 4 bars instrumental]

durationDesign.method: three full rap verses plus three hooks and bridge; 92 BPM protected by substantial vocal content

killingPointDesign.mechanism: count-like guitar harmonics plus cello rise
killingPointDesign.finalVariation: two people count together in final section

songs.lyrics:
[Intro - 8 bars instrumental]

[Verse 1 - 16 bars, sing-rap]
Playground gate unlocked, nobody inside,
one swing moving because the wind insists.
You say five o'clock used to mean one more game,
six meant somebody's voice from a balcony.
The slide got replaced, the sand became rubber,
but the fence still bends near the same corner.
You point to where everyone dropped their bags,
like the ground kept the arrangement memorized.
A basketball rolls from somewhere unseen,
stops at the fence and waits there.
You say that would have started another game once,
now nobody bothers to climb over.

[Pre-Hook - 8 bars]
The street got quieter as we got older,
or maybe we finally learned to hear it.
One swing, one ball, one light above the gate,
enough to restart the whole afternoon.

[Hook 1 - 12 bars]
After the Bell,
the day still had another hour.
After the Bell,
no one wanted to be first going home.
After the Bell,
the fence was only a suggestion.

[Verse 2 - 16 bars, sing-rap]
You tell me who always brought the ball,
who never remembered where a jacket went.
A balcony voice would call one name,
then two more children vanished with it.
I tell you my version had a rusted goalpost,
one ball shared by whoever arrived first.
You say every town apparently had the same rule,
and the empty playground feels less like yours alone.
We stand outside instead of going in,
which somehow makes the memory sharper.

[Hook 2 - 12 bars]
After the Bell,
one more game before the windows lit.
After the Bell,
we thought an hour was almost endless.
After the Bell,
now it fits inside a few lines.

[Bridge - 12 bars, sing-rap]
Muted trumpet holds two warm notes,
not copying any bell, just leaving space.
You say you can still hear the old noise,
I say the quiet tells me enough.
A kid runs past the far end of the fence,
and for a second the timing lines up.

[Verse 3 - 16 bars, sing-rap]
We leave just as the streetlights wake,
playground still empty behind us.
You tell one final story about losing a shoe,
winning anyway because everyone changed the rules.
I tell you that sounds suspicious,
you say history belongs to whoever remembers longer.
The microhouse pulse keeps the walking pace,
soft enough that the story remains first.

[Final Hook - 16 bars]
After the Bell,
[Male low response: one more hour]
After the Bell,
the day kept going because you did.
After the Bell,
trumpet holds the last word after the voice lets go.

[Outro - 4 bars instrumental]

killingPointDesign.mechanism: male response plus two-note trumpet sustain
killingPointDesign.finalVariation: final hook reframes the extra hour as memory

You stop at a window crowded with stickers,
stars, animals, letters in bubble print.
You say you spent everything on the shiny ones,
then traded half before going home.
Some were too good to stick anywhere,
so they lived for months inside a pencil case.
You remember the silver border best,
and one tiny planet that never peeled straight.
The shop light turns the glass slightly green,
and every sticker looks more expensive than it is.

[Male] Window Full
[Female] of Stickers

Blue paper, red binding, gold letters,

We argue gently over which habit is worse,

[Male] Good enough for tonight.

[Female] Window Full
[Male] of Stickers

Catch the bus, still walk two.

Last One Home,
twenty-three under the streetlight.

I tell you my bus number was seven,
you say every childhood needs one number too large in memory.

You remember winter windows fogged white,
names drawn once and erased by a sleeve.
I remember counting stops by shops,

Last One Home,
last bus before the alleys took over.
Last One Home,
one small number holding the route.

That route is next, so we stand,

No one is last home tonight,
we are only passing through the old rule.

[Final Hook - 12 bars]
Last One Home,
the vibraphone answers three small notes.
Not last tonight, just last back then.
Last One Home,
twenty-three still glowing when we turn.
